title: Projective space over Z represents invertible modules with generating sections
statement: Let $n\ge0$, let $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathbf Z[T_0,\dots,T_n])$ with $\deg T_i=1$, and let $\mathcal O(1)=\widetilde{S(1)}$ be its twisting sheaf (Stacks 01MM; canonically the module glued from the $\mathcal O_{D_+(T_j)}e_j$ by $e_i=(T_i/T_j)e_j$ of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]), with the global sections $T_0,\dots,T_n$ ($T_l\mapsto T_l/1\in(S_f)_1$ on every $D_+(f)$). Pullbacks $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)$, $\psi^*T_i$ are those of [def-pc-module-pullback]. For a scheme $Y$, consider pairs $(\mathcal L,(s_0,\dots,s_n))$ of an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and global sections $s_0,\dots,s_n\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ that generate $\mathcal L$ (for every $y\in Y$ some $s_i$ has nonzero image in $\mathcal L_y\otimes\kappa(y)$), up to the equivalence $(\mathcal L,(s_i))\sim(\mathcal N,(t_i))$ iff there is an isomorphism $\beta:\mathcal L\to\mathcal N$ with $\beta(s_i)=t_i$ for all $i$. Then for every such pair there is a unique morphism $\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}:Y\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ with an isomorphism $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L$ carrying $\psi^*T_i$ to $s_i$ for all $i$; equivalent pairs give the same morphism, every morphism $Y\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ arises in this way, and the construction is compatible with pullback along morphisms $Y'\to Y$. That is, $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ represents the functor $Y\mapsto\{(\mathcal L,(s_0,\dots,s_n))\}/\sim$ [def-pc-representable-functor].

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 27.13.1 (Tag 01NE, label lemma-projective-space), proved there as the special case of Lemma 01NA (label lemma-apply), itself a reformulation of Lemma 01N9 (label lemma-proj-functor-strict)

proof.text: *The charts.* Let $S=\mathbf Z[T_0,\dots,T_n]$. Since $T_0,\dots,T_n$ are homogeneous of degree one and generate $S_+$, the standard opens $D_+(T_j)$ cover $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ and $D_+(T_j)\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_{(T_j)}$ [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts]: $\mathcal O(1)$ is invertible; $S_{(T_j)}=\mathbf Z[T_0/T_j,\dots,T_n/T_j]$ is the polynomial ring in the $T_l/T_j$ ($l\neq j$), in particular generated by them; $D_+(T_j)$ is the non-vanishing locus of $T_j$; and $T_l=(T_l/T_j)\,T_j$ on $D_+(T_j)$. Hence (by [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes]) $T_j|_{D_+(T_j)}$ is a basis of $\mathcal O(1)|_{D_+(T_j)}$. Two consequences, elementary from these: (b1) $D_+(T_j)\cap D_+(T_k)$ is the locus of $D_+(T_j)$ where $T_k/T_j$ is invertible: on $D_+(T_j)$, $T_k=(T_k/T_j)T_j$ with $T_j$ a basis, so $T_k$ does not vanish at $x$ iff the germ of $T_k/T_j$ is a unit, and $D_+(T_k)$ is the non-vanishing locus of $T_k$; (b2) on $D_+(T_j)\cap D_+(T_k)$, $(T_l/T_k)(T_k/T_j)T_j=(T_l/T_k)T_k=T_l=(T_l/T_j)T_j$, so $T_l/T_j=(T_l/T_k)(T_k/T_j)$ by uniqueness of coefficients with respect to the basis $T_j$ (in particular $(T_j/T_k)(T_k/T_j)=1$).

source.place: Lemma 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space); Section 27.10 (01MM); Lemma 01M4; proof of Lemma 01N8, first and second paragraphs

proof.text: *The pieces $Y_{s_j}$ and the functions $s_l/s_j$.* Let $(\mathcal L,(s_0,\dots,s_n))$ be a pair as in the statement. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] each $Y_{s_j}=\{y:\ s_j(y)\neq0\}$ is open and $s_j$ trivializes $\mathcal L|_{Y_{s_j}}$; since the $s_i$ generate, the $Y_{s_j}$ cover $Y$ (this is the hypothesis of the statement, equivalently [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre] for the sheaf-theoretic notion of generation). Put $a^{(j)}_l=s_l/s_j\in\Gamma(Y_{s_j},\mathcal O_Y)$, the unique function with $s_l=a^{(j)}_ls_j$ on $Y_{s_j}$; so $a^{(j)}_j=1$. On $V_{jk}=Y_{s_j}\cap Y_{s_k}$: $s_j=a^{(k)}_ja^{(j)}_ks_j$ and $s_l=a^{(k)}_la^{(j)}_ks_j$, so by uniqueness of the quotient $a^{(k)}_ja^{(j)}_k=1$ and $a^{(j)}_l=a^{(k)}_l\,(a^{(k)}_j)^{-1}$; and $Y_{s_k}\cap Y_{s_j}$ is the locus of $Y_{s_k}$ where $a^{(k)}_j$ is invertible: at $y\in Y_{s_k}$, $s_k$ generates the free rank-one module $\mathcal L_y$, so $s_j=a^{(k)}_js_k$ lies outside $\mathfrak m_y\mathcal L_y$ iff $a^{(k)}_j\notin\mathfrak m_y$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), first two paragraphs; Modules, Lemma 01CY

proof.text: *The local morphisms $\psi_j$.* The ring map $\mathbf Z[T_0,\dots,T_n]\to\Gamma(Y_{s_j},\mathcal O_Y)$, $T_l\mapsto a^{(j)}_l$ (universal property of the polynomial ring) sends $T_j$ to $a^{(j)}_j=1$, hence extends uniquely to $S[1/T_j]$; its restriction to the degree-zero subring is a ring map $\rho_j:S_{(T_j)}\to\Gamma(Y_{s_j},\mathcal O_Y)$ with $\rho_j(T_l/T_j)=a^{(j)}_l$ (on $a/T_j^m$ it is $\psi(a)/s_j^m$, Stacks' formula, with $\psi(a)$ the value of the form $a$ at the $s_i$); by the generation in step 1 it is the only ring map with these values. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] $\rho_j$ corresponds to a unique morphism $\psi_j:Y_{s_j}\to\operatorname{Spec}S_{(T_j)}=D_+(T_j)\subseteq\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ with $\psi_j^\sharp=\rho_j$, and $\psi_j^{-1}$ of the locus where $T_k/T_j$ is invertible is the locus where $a^{(j)}_k$ is invertible, i.e. $\psi_j^{-1}(D_+(T_j)\cap D_+(T_k))=Y_{s_j}\cap Y_{s_k}$ (step 2).

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8: 'define a ring map $\psi_{(f)}:S_{(f)}\to\Gamma(Y_s,\mathcal O_Y)$ by $a/f^n\mapsto\psi(a)/s^n$ ... corresponds to a morphism $\varphi_f:Y_s\to D_+(f)$'; Schemes, Lemmas 01I1, 01HY

proof.text: *Agreement on overlaps.* Let $V=Y_{s_j}\cap Y_{s_k}$. By step 3 (for $k$ and for $j$) both $\psi_j|_V$ and $\psi_k|_V$ map $V$ into $D_+(T_j)\cap D_+(T_k)\subseteq D_+(T_j)=\operatorname{Spec}S_{(T_j)}$, so both are morphisms $V\to\operatorname{Spec}S_{(T_j)}$, determined by their ring maps $S_{(T_j)}\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], hence by the images of the generators $T_l/T_j$ (step 1). For $\psi_j$ the image is $a^{(j)}_l|_V$. For $\psi_k$, use $T_l/T_j=(T_l/T_k)\,(T_j/T_k)^{-1}$ on $D_+(T_j)\cap D_+(T_k)$ (step 1) and that $\psi_k^\sharp$ is a ring map compatible with restriction: the image is $a^{(k)}_l\,(a^{(k)}_j)^{-1}|_V$, which equals $a^{(j)}_l|_V$ by step 2. Hence $\psi_j|_V=\psi_k|_V$. (Stacks argues the same identity with the ring $S_{(T_jT_k)}$ and the separatedness of Proj; the computation of images of generators is that argument written out.)

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8, second paragraph ('the rule $x/(ff')^n\mapsto\psi(x)/(ss')^n$ ... the morphisms $\varphi_f$ and $\varphi_{f'}$ agree over $Y_s\cap Y_{s'}$')

proof.text: *Gluing $\psi$.* By step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] the $\psi_j$ glue to a unique morphism $\psi:Y\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ with $\psi|_{Y_{s_j}}=\psi_j$ for all $j$. Moreover $\psi^{-1}(D_+(T_j))=Y_{s_j}$: '$\supseteq$' as $\psi_j$ lands in $D_+(T_j)$; for '$\subseteq$', a point $y$ with $\psi(y)\in D_+(T_j)$ lies in some $Y_{s_k}$, and then $\psi_k(y)\in D_+(T_j)\cap D_+(T_k)$, so $y\in Y_{s_j}\cap Y_{s_k}$ by step 3.

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8: 'the morphisms $\psi_f$ glue to a global morphism'

proof.text: *The isomorphism $\alpha:\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\to\mathcal L$.* $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)$ is invertible [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible], and for an $\mathcal O$-module $\mathcal F$, a function $f$ and a section $t$ one has $\psi^*(ft)=\psi^\sharp(f)\,\psi^*t$ and $(\psi^*\mathcal F)|_{\psi^{-1}W}=(\psi|)^*(\mathcal F|_W)$, $\psi^*\mathcal O=\mathcal O$ with $\psi^*1=1$ (definition of the pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] as $\psi^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{\psi^{-1}\mathcal O}\mathcal O_Y$). Since $T_j|_{D_+(T_j)}$ is a basis of $\mathcal O(1)|_{D_+(T_j)}$ (step 1) and $\psi(Y_{s_j})\subseteq D_+(T_j)$, $(\psi^*\mathcal O(1))|_{Y_{s_j}}$ is free with basis $\psi^*T_j$, and $\mathcal L|_{Y_{s_j}}$ is free with basis $s_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes]. Let $\alpha_j$ be the isomorphism sending $\psi^*T_j$ to $s_j$. Then $\alpha_j(\psi^*T_l)=\alpha_j(\psi^\sharp(T_l/T_j)\psi^*T_j)=a^{(j)}_ls_j=s_l$ on $Y_{s_j}$ for all $l$. On $Y_{s_j}\cap Y_{s_k}$ both $\alpha_j$ and $\alpha_k$ are $\mathcal O$-linear and send $\psi^*T_k$, a basis there, to $s_k$; so they agree. Since $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_Y}(\psi^*\mathcal O(1),\mathcal L)$ is a sheaf on (the Zariski site of) $Y$ [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-is-sheaf], the compatible family $(\alpha_j)$ glues to a unique $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $\alpha:\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\to\mathcal L$ with $\alpha|_{Y_{s_j}}=\alpha_j$; likewise the inverses $\alpha_j^{-1}$ (also compatible) glue to some $\alpha'$, and $\alpha'\alpha$, $\alpha\alpha'$ restrict to identities on every $Y_{s_j}$, so equal the identities by the uniqueness of gluing: $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. Finally $\alpha(\psi^*T_i)$ and $s_i$ are sections of the sheaf $\mathcal L$ agreeing on every $Y_{s_j}$, so $\alpha(\psi^*T_i)=s_i$ for all $i$. This proves existence.

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8: 'the isomorphism $\alpha_f$ which maps the pullback of the trivializing section $f$ to $s$ ... the maps $\alpha_f$ glue'

proof.text: *Uniqueness.* Let $\psi':Y\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ and $\alpha':\psi'^*\mathcal O(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L$ with $\alpha'(\psi'^*T_i)=s_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (3), $(\psi'^*T_j)(y)=T_j(\psi'(y))\otimes1$, so the non-vanishing locus of $\psi'^*T_j$ is $\psi'^{-1}$ of that of $T_j$, which is $\psi'^{-1}(D_+(T_j))$ (step 1, (d)); and the isomorphism $\alpha'$ carries it to the non-vanishing locus of $s_j$ (an isomorphism $\alpha'$ of invertible modules induces isomorphisms $\mathcal L'_y\to\mathcal L_y$ carrying $\mathfrak m_y\mathcal L'_y$ onto $\mathfrak m_y\mathcal L_y$). Hence $\psi'^{-1}(D_+(T_j))=Y_{s_j}$. On $Y_{s_j}$ pull back $T_l=(T_l/T_j)T_j$ (step 1): $\psi'^*T_l=\psi'^\sharp(T_l/T_j)\,\psi'^*T_j$, and applying $\alpha'$, $s_l=\psi'^\sharp(T_l/T_j)\,s_j$, so $\psi'^\sharp(T_l/T_j)=s_l/s_j=a^{(j)}_l$ by uniqueness of the quotient. Thus $\psi'|_{Y_{s_j}}:Y_{s_j}\to D_+(T_j)=\operatorname{Spec}S_{(T_j)}$ has a ring map agreeing with $\rho_j$ on the generators $T_l/T_j$, so it equals $\psi_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. As the $Y_{s_j}$ cover $Y$, $\psi'=\psi$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing].

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8, last paragraph ('the inverse images of $D_+(f)$ under both $\varphi$ and $\varphi'$ are equal to $Y_{\psi(f)}$ ... $\varphi^\sharp(x/f^n)=(\varphi')^\sharp(x/f^n)$ ... Hence $\varphi$ and $\varphi'$ are the same')

proof.text: *Equivalent pairs, and every morphism arises.* If $\beta:\mathcal L\to\mathcal N$ is an isomorphism with $\beta(s_i)=t_i$, then $\beta\circ\alpha:\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\to\mathcal N$ carries $\psi^*T_i$ to $t_i$, so by uniqueness $\psi_{(\mathcal N,(t_i))}=\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}$. Conversely let $\varphi:Y\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ be any morphism. $\varphi^*\mathcal O(1)$ is invertible [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-invertible], and the sections $\varphi^*T_i$ generate it in the fibre sense: for $y\in Y$ choose $j$ with $\varphi(y)\in D_+(T_j)$ (step 1); then $(\varphi^*T_j)(y)=T_j(\varphi(y))\otimes1\neq0$ [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (3). With $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi$ has the defining property for the pair $(\varphi^*\mathcal O(1),(\varphi^*T_i))$, so $\varphi=\psi_{(\varphi^*\mathcal O(1),(\varphi^*T_i))}$ by uniqueness.

source.place: Lemma 01N9 (lemma-proj-functor-strict: $(\mathcal O(d),\psi^d)$ is the universal family) and Lemma 01NA, specialized as in the proof of Lemma 01NE

proof.text: *Compatibility with pullback, and representability.* Let $h:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism. The pulled-back pair $(h^*\mathcal L,(h^*s_i))$ is again a pair: $h^*\mathcal L$ is invertible and $(h^*s_i)(y')=s_i(h(y'))\otimes1$ [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (1), (3), so some $h^*s_i$ is nonzero at each $y'$. The canonical isomorphism $(\psi\circ h)^*\mathcal O(1)\cong h^*\psi^*\mathcal O(1)$ sending $(\psi h)^*T_i$ to $h^*\psi^*T_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] (2), followed by $h^*\alpha$, is an isomorphism $(\psi h)^*\mathcal O(1)\to h^*\mathcal L$ sending $(\psi h)^*T_i$ to $h^*s_i$; by uniqueness $\psi_{(h^*\mathcal L,(h^*s_i))}=\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}\circ h$. Hence $F(Y)=\{(\mathcal L,(s_i))\}/\!\sim$ is a functor (pullback respects $\sim$: $h^*\beta$), the maps $F(Y)\to\operatorname{Mor}(Y,\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z})$, $[(\mathcal L,(s_i))]\mapsto\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}$, are well defined (step 8), natural in $Y$ (this step), surjective (step 8) and injective (if $\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}=\psi_{(\mathcal N,(t_i))}=\psi$ with isomorphisms $\alpha,\alpha'$, then $\beta=\alpha'\circ\alpha^{-1}$ carries $s_i$ to $t_i$). So $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ represents $F$ [def-pc-representable-functor], with universal pair $(\mathcal O(1),(T_0,\dots,T_n))$.
